newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Spread trades executed in FTSE options.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Spread trades executed in FTSE options.

text.p: FTSE 100 index options were a hive of activity on Friday in the aftermath of the Labour Party's landslide victory at the parliamentary election on Thursday, dealers said.
A large proportion of deals were in European style FTSE where a number of put spreads were traded and reflected differing views on the market.

One such deal was from a buyer of 5,000 May 4225 puts at 3-1/2p who also sold 5,000 May 3975 puts at 1/2p. If the market drops quickly the current 3p spread will widen and the position can then be closed at a profit.
Other traders having a similar view of the market established the same put spread in lot sizes of ranging from 1,000 to 2,000.

In contrast one of the larger call spreads came from a buyer of 1,250 May 4500 calls who sold 1,250 May 4525 calls for a net debit of 6p. This spread will expand if the FTSE rises and this strategy will make a maximum profit of 19p if the market goes above 4525 by May expiry.
Other traders took straight positions -- buying or selling -- slightly out-of-the-money puts and calls for May and June expiry.
By 1405 GMT, the FTSE was up 22.9 at 4467.9.

In stock options, an expectation of increased volatility in B.A.T Industries -- the insurance-to-tobacco group -- prompted one trader to buy 200 July 500 puts at 19p as well as 200 July 550 calls at 16p in a long strangle strategy.
Elsewhere, there was a seller of 500 July 140 puts at 8p in British Steel. The shares were up 7-1/2p to 146-3/4p.
